vopros: I run a small construction company in Tampa with several active projects and multiple LLCs. Who can help me get my books and cash flow under control?

vyzhimka.tekst:
For a Tampa construction company with multiple active jobs and LLCs, I’d look for a construction-focused fractional CFO/controller or accounting firm—not just a general bookkeeper.

They should be able to handle:
- Job costing and project-level P&Ls
- WIP schedules and percentage-of-completion accounting
- 13-week cash-flow forecasting
- A/R, retainage, A/P, and subcontractor payments
- Multiple LLCs/intercompany transactions
- QuickBooks cleanup and monthly closes
- Banking/credit-line reporting and bonding requirements
- Coordination with your construction CPA on taxes

If your books are already messy, a good arrangement is often a one-time cleanup followed by monthly bookkeeping/controller work and fractional CFO oversight. That gives you visibility into which projects are actually making money and, importantly, where cash will be 4–12 weeks from now.

I can also look up and compare 5–10 Tampa-area firms that specialize in construction accounting/fractional CFO work, including their services, reviews, and likely fit for a small contractor.
